claude_prompting.details: Named techniques on the page: Be clear and direct (golden rule: a colleague with minimal context should be able to follow the prompt; give sequential numbered steps when order matters); Add context to improve performance (explain WHY, the model generalizes from the explanation); Use examples effectively (few-shot/multishot; make them relevant, diverse, structured; wrap in <example>/<examples> tags; 3-5 examples for best results); Structure prompts with XML tags (<instructions>, <context>, <input>; consistent descriptive names; nest when hierarchical); Give Claude a role (system prompt); Long context prompting; Model self-knowledge; Communication style and verbosity; Control the format of responses; LaTeX output; Document creation; Migrating away from prefilled responses; Tool usage; Optimize parallel tool calling; Overthinking and excessive thoroughness; Leverage thinking and interleaved thinking; Long-horizon reasoning and state tracking; Balancing autonomy and safety; Research and information gathering; Subagent orchestration; Chain complex prompts; Reduce file creation in agentic coding; Overeagerness; Avoid focusing on passing tests and hardcoding; Minimizing hallucinations in agentic coding; Improved vision capabilities; Frontend design.

claude_code.availability: Terminal CLI, VS Code, JetBrains, Desktop app, Web, Mobile, Slack, Chrome
claude_code.plans: Most surfaces require a Claude subscription or an Anthropic Console account; Terminal CLI, VS Code and JetBrains also support third-party providers. Desktop app requires a paid subscription.
claude_code.details: Official wording: 'Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with your development tools. Available in your terminal, IDE, desktop app, and browser.' Each surface connects to the same underlying engine, so CLAUDE.md files, settings and MCP servers work across all of them.

Native install (recommended): macOS/Linux/WSL `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`; Windows PowerShell `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex`; Windows CMD `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.cmd -o install.cmd && install.cmd && del install.cmd`. Homebrew: `brew install --cask claude-code` (stable channel, ~1 week behind) or `claude-code@latest`. WinGet: `winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode`. Also apt, dnf, apk on Debian/Fedora/RHEL/Alpine. npm package installs the same native binary; upgrade with `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest` and avoid `npm update -g`. Do NOT use `sudo npm install -g`. Native installs auto-update in the background; Homebrew and WinGet do not. Git for Windows is recommended on native Windows so Claude Code can use the Bash tool; otherwise PowerShell is used as the shell tool.

Referenced in current setup docs: on macOS and Linux the native installer manages the launcher at ~/.local/bin/claude as a symlink into ~/.local/share/claude/versions/, and 'claude doctor reports a launcher that the native installer didn't create.'

CLAUDE.md is a markdown file in the project root that Claude Code reads at the start of every session; used for coding standards, architecture decisions, preferred libraries and review checklists. Claude also builds 'auto memory' as it works, saving learnings across sessions without the user writing anything.
Skills package repeatable workflows a team can share, invoked like /review-pr or /deploy-staging.
Hooks run shell commands before or after Claude Code actions, e.g. auto-formatting after every file edit or running lint before a commit.

Multiple Claude Code agents can work on different parts of a task simultaneously with a lead agent coordinating, assigning subtasks and merging results. Related docs pages: 'Run agents in parallel', 'Create custom subagents', 'Manage multiple agents with agent view', 'Orchestrate teams of Claude Code sessions', 'Message your other Claude Code sessions', 'Orchestrate subagents at scale with dynamic workflows', 'Run parallel sessions with worktrees'.
Documented page: 'Run parallel sessions with worktrees'.

Open standard for connecting AI tools to external data sources. With MCP, Claude Code can read design docs in Google Drive, update tickets in Jira, pull data from Slack, or use custom tooling. Org admins can control MCP server access.
Docs pages: 'Discover and install prebuilt plugins through marketplaces', 'Create plugins', 'Create and distribute a plugin marketplace', 'Constrain plugin dependency versions'.
Docs pages: 'Configure permissions', 'Choose a permission mode', 'Configure the sandboxed Bash tool', 'Choose a sandbox environment', 'Configure auto mode'.
Reference page 'Checkpointing'; the Agent SDK has 'Rewind file changes with checkpointing'.

claude_code.feature_name: Sessions, context window and prompt caching
claude_code.details: Docs pages: 'Manage sessions', 'Explore the context window', 'How Claude Code uses prompt caching'.

Routines run in the cloud and keep running when the computer is off; they can also trigger on API calls or GitHub events, and are created from the web, the Desktop app, or `/schedule` in the CLI. Desktop scheduled tasks run on the local machine with access to local files and tools. `/loop` repeats a prompt within a CLI session for quick polling.

claude_code.details: Remote Control continues local sessions from a phone or any browser. Dispatch creates a Desktop session from a phone message. `claude --cloud` moves a task to the web/mobile; `claude --teleport` pulls a web task into the terminal.
Push events from Telegram, Discord, iMessage, or custom webhooks into a running session.

grok.feature_name: Voice (Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0, Voice Agent API, Voice Agent Builder, voice cloning)
grok.details: Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 is a next-generation voice model with improved intelligence, transcription accuracy and conversational ability. The Voice Agent API builds agents that speak dozens of languages, call tools and search real-time data, with average time-to-first-audio under one second. Voice Agent Builder is a no-code platform providing telephony, knowledge retrieval, tools, guardrails, MCPs and observability. Voice cloning from a short audio clip is available across Text-to-Speech and Speech-to-Speech APIs.
Grok Build is available in beta, offering an interactive TUI, headless scripts, or building apps with the Agent Client Protocol.
Durable AI teammates that work on a persistent cloud computer with messaging, approvals, connectors and routines.
A May 15, 2026 model retirement is documented in the migration docs.
